title: What happens if you override equals() but not hashCode()?
shortTitle: What happens if you override equals() but not hashCode()?
keyPoints: Objects that are equals() will have different hashCode values → violates the contract
HashMap.get() looks in the WRONG bucket → returns null even though the key is logically present
HashSet.contains() returns false for an equal object
The object is effectively lost in any hash-based collection
SpotBugs/SonarQube flag this as a critical bug

s1_definition.oneliner: HashMap and HashSet break silently. Equal objects land in different buckets because their hash codes differ, so lookups return null and contains returns false.
s1_definition.profdef:
The consequence:

- **HashMap.get() fails.** It computes hashCode of the lookup key, goes to that bucket, and never finds the stored object (which is in a different bucket because its hashCode was computed with Object's default).
- **HashSet.contains() fails.** Same reason – wrong bucket.
- **The object is present but unfindable.** It is a silent, hard-to-debug data loss.
s1_definition.analogy: Filing an account in drawer A (default hashCode) but searching in drawer B (equals-based hashCode). The account is there, but you are looking in the wrong place.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Without hashCode override:
    a = new Account("SAV2001")   hashCode = 12345 (memory-based)
    b = new Account("SAV2001")   hashCode = 67890 (different memory)
    a.equals(b) = true           but hashCode differs!

  HashMap:
    put(a, "Rajesh")  → bucket 12345 % capacity = bucket 5
    get(b)            → bucket 67890 % capacity = bucket 10  ← WRONG bucket
    → returns null (object lost!)

  Fix: override hashCode to use accountId.hashCode()
    → both hash to same bucket → equals finds the match
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Overriding equals() without hashCode() breaks HashMap and HashSet. Equal objects get different hash codes, land in different buckets, and become unfindable. The object is present but the lookup misses it.

Always override both together using the same fields. Use Objects.hash(), IDE generation, records, or Lombok.

One sentence to remember: override equals without hashCode and your objects vanish from HashMap – always override both together.
